title: Correctness of the merge procedure
statement: Let a program $P$ contain the merge procedure at position $p$, and let the machine limits have word bound $W$, memory size $S$, and depth bound $D$. Suppose the input memory $\mu$ stores lists $l,r$ of integers starting at addresses $a,b$, respectively; both lists and a destination segment of length $|l|+|r|$ fit within memory; the destination segment is disjoint from each input segment; and $S\le W$. Then, when the procedure is called at depth $d$ with inputs $(a,|l|,b,|r|,\mathrm{dst})$, it can execute within time $40(|l|+|r|)+12$ and leave a memory $\mu'$ in which the segment starting at $\mathrm{dst}$ contains the sorted merge of $l$ and $r$, while every memory location outside that destination segment retains its initial value.
hypotheses_covered: The program has the merge procedure at index $p$
The machine limits $\mathrm{lim}$ and depth $d$ are fixed
The initial memory contains $l$ at $a$ and $r$ at $b$
The segment at $a$ is disjoint from the destination segment
The segment at $b$ is disjoint from the destination segment
